==== tluaUncheckedIndexedAccessDefault.tlua (3 errors) ====
    // Indexing a key a table does not have yields nil in Lua, so an index read widens to
    // `V | nil` with nothing to switch on: noUncheckedIndexedAccess is the default here.
    // In TypeScript the option is a strictness opt-in; for Lua it is plain accuracy, so it
    // does not follow `strict` either.
    
    interface Registry { [key: string]: number }
    declare reg: Registry;
    local direct: number | nil = reg["a"];
    local wrong: number = reg["a"];
          ~~~~~
!!! error TLUA2322: Type 'number | nil' is not assignable to type 'number'.
!!! error TLUA2322:   Type 'nil' is not assignable to type 'number'.
    
    // A number-key table is the same shape -- there is no length to index against -- so an
    // element read widens the same way.
    declare xs: number[];
    local first: number | nil = xs[1];
    
    // Which is the point: the widening is what gives a presence guard something to narrow.
    // Without it the condition would be the declared value type -- here the literal `true` --
    // and the guard would prove nothing.
    local queue: Table<string, true> = {};
    if queue["k"] then
      local seen: true = queue["k"];
    end
    
    // A declared property is not an index signature and keeps its exact type; only the keys
    // the index signature opens are the ones that might not be there.
    interface Named { label: string; [key: string]: string }
    declare named: Named;
    local label: string = named.label;
    local other: string | nil = named["other"];
    
    // It is a read-position rule: a write still takes the declared value type.
    reg["a"] = 1;
    
    // A union can answer the same key from a declared property in one arm and an index
    // signature in another. The index-signature arm may hold no such key, so the read is
    // possibly nil -- through both spellings of the access, which must always agree.
    declare mixed: Registry | { a: boolean };
    local viaIndex: number | boolean | nil = mixed["a"];
    local viaDot: number | boolean | nil = mixed.a;
    local viaIndexUnsafe: number | boolean = mixed["a"];
